subject.summary: Original crewed ring-ice pusher. Long compression spine, raised two-deck bow cab, articulated four-jaw empty cradle and thrust-parallel folding radiators. An engineering-informed game design, not a flight-qualified spacecraft.

sources.title: NASA-CR-114938: Reusable Space Tug, spacecraft concepts and systems design, 1971
NASA NTRS 20000032541: Thermal Radiator Pointing for International Space Station (1999)

rounds.summary: The requested two-deck panoramic cab is identifiable as a cabin but its close view reads as a stack of similarly weighted horizontal loops.

The broad bow platen and its four square contact regions remain mostly featureless rectangles, especially beside the articulated jaw roots a
No further defect requested in this round.

The contact assemblies remain straight rectangular stacks: one broad open-looking box, a narrow central block, and a detached-looking end bl
The four engine bell and gimbal units are distinct, but their broad polygonal backing plates visually merge into the central aft framework;
The tank end hoops and small lower plates are visible, but the restraint-to-spine attachment remains a thin, abrupt meeting of large hoop an
Each of the three broad ice-contact lands is a largely featureless chamfered slab. The small peripheral fasteners and carrier pivot are purp

The long tank barrels between the developed end hoops remain mostly empty straight-sided spans, with isolated small boxes and no legible con
No further defect requested in this round.

how: Original fictional spacecraft designed for the supplied game brief.
NASA modular-tug, ISS truss and thermal-control reasoning informs the architecture; no vehicle is copied.
Every vessel dimension and hardware shape is designed/inferred. No flight-performance claim is made.
